responses.ensemble_reason: I kept the single Logistic Regression model. It had the highest mean AP across the three forward folds: 0.392 (fold SD 0.030), compared with 0.389 for the weighted average, 0.383 for stacking, and 0.372 for equal averaging. The ensembles' AP lifts over Logistic were zero or negative, and none passed the worth-it gate. The differences are also much smaller than the fold SD, so I can't claim an ensemble is better. Logistic's Brier score was 0.0633 and ECE was 0.0188. Stacking had a worse ECE of 0.0311; the weighted average's ECE was slightly lower at 0.0177, but it still had no AP gain. The ensembles require more models and, for stacking, a meta-model, so the extra complexity wasn't justified.
responses.validation_limits: I excluded the leaky days_past_due_60 field. The nested forward OOF comparison used 2,155 predictions from three later-period folds. Training rows were old enough for their 90-day labels to mature, validation customers were kept out of training, and ensemble weights and the stacker were learned from inner OOF predictions only. There were no outer OOF predictions for the warm-up rows, so 2,155 of the 6,576 fit-and-selection rows were evaluated. There were only three folds, and their training histories overlap. The fold SD of about 0.03 is similar to the differences between the top models; it is descriptive, not a confidence interval. The threshold and loss were also selected on these OOF predictions, so they are development results, not an independent final test. The data are synthetic, and the course had used the training data earlier.
responses.calibration_limits: The sigmoid mapping was fitted using 836 reserved calibration rows, including 78 positives from July–September 2024. The reported scores are on those same rows, so they are fit diagnostics, not an independent test. AP stayed at 0.2878 and ROC-AUC at 0.7890, as expected for a monotonic mapping. The other scores got worse: Brier changed from 0.0765 to 0.0781, ECE from 0.0211 to 0.0349, and log loss from 0.2665 to 0.2773. So these results don't show that calibration improved. I would need separate labeled data to evaluate calibration independently. Challenge labels are unavailable.
responses.capacity_fairness: The OOF-selected raw threshold was 0.1689. It flagged 245 of 2,155 requests (11.4%); the highest period-level flag fraction was 11.7%, within the 12% limit. The threshold's OOF loss was 1,111 fictional teaching units. The regional OOF false-positive rates were Central 7.98% (489 negatives), Western 10.29% (486), Eastern 6.31% (507), and Other 8.10% (494). That is a 3.98 percentage-point gap, with recall ranging from 44.7% in Western to 50.0% in Central. For the full challenge batch, the transported threshold was 0.1223: 330 of 2,500 requests were above it, so the 300-request cap removed 30 flags. The boundary score was 0.1299, and equal-score blocks were not split. The regional results are descriptive only: there are no confidence intervals and they are not a fairness certification. Challenge labels are unavailable, so I can't calculate challenge false-positive rates or check the regional mix of actual errors.
responses.explanation_scope: No. Day 4's SHAP, permutation importance, reason codes, and review zone explain the class-weighted LightGBM model (80 trees), not the final Day 5 Logistic Regression model. In Day 4, “weighted” referred to class weights; in Day 5, the weighted average is an ensemble. I can't carry Day 4's explanations over as claims about the final model. I would recheck global importance and local reason codes using the final model, then check explanations around the new calibrated threshold of 0.1223.
responses.intended_use: This is for a fictional training exercise using synthetic Tamweel Lite data. A 1 means a simulated request for human review; a 0 is not a safety guarantee or financing approval. I would not use it to score real people or make real loan approval, rejection, pricing, or eligibility decisions. The data are synthetic, the loss units are educational, and the model has not been certified as fair.
responses.monitoring_plan: I would monitor changes in key inputs such as bureau_score and dti, missing values, and the score distribution. As 90-day labels mature, I would check AP by period, Brier, ECE, and observed default rates by probability bin. I would also track how many requests exceed the 0.1223 threshold, how many the 300-request cap removes, and regional flag and false-positive rates with their denominators. The Western–Eastern false-positive gap in this run was 3.98 percentage points, so I would watch whether it persists. I would set review or retraining triggers in advance and investigate them using labeled data, rather than judging performance from the unlabeled challenge set.
responses.executive_summary_ar: اخترت Logistic Regression كنموذج نهائي مفرد. حقق أعلى متوسط AP في نتائج OOF الأمامية المتداخلة: 0.392 عبر ثلاث طيات، مقابل 0.389 للمتوسط الموزون و0.383 للـStacking و0.372 للمتوسط المتساوي. لم يجتز أي تجميع بوابة الجدوى، لذلك لم يبرر التعقيد الإضافي استخدامه. في دفعة التحدي، تجاوزت 330 من أصل 2,500 طلب العتبة المنقولة 0.1223؛ وبعد تطبيق سقف 12% مرة واحدة، بقيت 300 إشارة مراجعة محاكاة وأُزيلت 30. ظهر فرق وصفي قدره 3.98 نقاط مئوية بين أعلى وأدنى معدل إنذار خاطئ إقليمي، ويحتاج إلى متابعة. البيانات اصطناعية، والنتائج للتدريب فقط وليست لقرارات تمويل حقيقية.
responses.executive_summary_en: I chose the single Logistic Regression model because it had the highest mean AP in the nested forward OOF results (0.392 across three folds). No ensemble passed the worth-it gate, so the extra complexity wasn't justified. On the 2,500-request challenge batch, 330 requests exceeded the transported threshold of 0.1223; applying the 12% capacity limit once left 300 simulated review flags and removed 30. The regional OOF false-positive gap was 3.98 percentage points and needs monitoring. The data are synthetic, so this is for training only, not real financing decisions.
